prompt: According to the section, what does spectrophotometry monitor when it is used to measure a reaction rate?

choices.text: The concentration of a light absorber
The heat given off as the reaction runs
choices.why: Heat is measured by calorimetry. Spectrophotometry monitors the concentration of a species that absorbs light.

choices.text: The pressure of any gas that is formed
choices.why: Spectrophotometry measures light, not pressure. It follows the concentration of a species that absorbs light.

choices.text: The mass of solid product formed
choices.why: Nothing is weighed. Spectrophotometry follows the concentration of a species that absorbs light as the reaction runs.

explanation: A common way to measure reaction rates is to use spectrophotometry to monitor the concentration of a species that absorbs light. As that species is used up or formed, the light it absorbs changes with it.

prompt: According to the section, why is it preferable, when possible, to measure the appearance of a product rather than the disappearance of a reactant?

choices.text: The background interference is low
Products always absorb more light
choices.why: The section doesn't say products absorb more. Its reason is the low background interference of a product measurement.

choices.text: Reactants cannot be seen by spectrophotometry
choices.why: A reactant that absorbs light can be followed too. A product is preferred because of the low background interference.

choices.text: Products form faster than reactants vanish
choices.why: The stoichiometry ties the two together; the section's reason is different. Following a product gives low background interference.

explanation: Following a product is preferred because of the low background interference of the measurement. Even so, the section notes that high-quality kinetic data can be obtained either way.

prompt: In a certain reaction only a reactant absorbs light, so the rate must be measured from its disappearance. According to the section, what can be expected?

choices.text: Good kinetic data can still be obtained
No useful rate data can be obtained
choices.why: Following a product is only preferred, not required. High-quality kinetic data can be obtained either way.

choices.text: Only the very first instant can be used
choices.why: Nothing limits a reactant measurement to the start. The section says high-quality kinetic data can be obtained either way.

choices.text: The orders found will equal the coefficients
choices.why: Orders come from the data, never from the coefficients. Following a reactant can still give high-quality kinetic data.

explanation: Measuring a product is preferable when possible, because of its low background interference. But the section notes that high-quality kinetic data can be obtained from a reactant or a product.

prompt: In the stopped-flow method, as the section describes it, what does the flow control, provided by syringes or valves, do?

choices.text: Drives the reactants into a mixing chamber
Keeps the reactants apart until the end
choices.why: The reactants are not kept apart: the flow control sends them into a mixing chamber, where the reaction takes place.

choices.text: Draws the products out as they form
choices.why: Nothing is drawn off. The flow control drives the reactants into a mixing chamber, where they react and are probed.

choices.text: Cools the reactants so they react slowly
choices.why: Flow control moves liquids; it does not cool them. It drives the reactants into a mixing chamber, where the reaction takes place.

explanation: Syringes or other valves control the flow of the reactants into a mixing chamber, where the reaction takes place. The reaction mixture can then be probed spectrophotometrically.

prompt: In the stopped-flow method, once the reactants meet in the mixing chamber, how does the section say the reaction mixture is followed?

choices.text: It is probed spectrophotometrically
Samples are taken out and weighed
choices.why: Nothing is taken out or weighed. The mixture in the chamber is probed spectrophotometrically, through the light it absorbs.

choices.text: Its temperature is logged over time
choices.why: The section doesn't follow the temperature. The reaction mixture is probed spectrophotometrically.

choices.text: Its volume is read off the syringes
choices.why: The syringes only control the flow. The reaction mixture is followed by probing it spectrophotometrically.

explanation: After the reactants are driven into the mixing chamber, the reaction mixture can be probed spectrophotometrically. Stopped-flow methods are commonly used in physical chemistry laboratory courses.

prompt: According to the section, why can methods based on the initial rate of a reaction carry a great deal of experimental uncertainty?

choices.text: Instruments or conditions fluctuate
The reactants have not yet been mixed
choices.why: The rate is measured once the reaction is running. The section blames fluctuations in instrumentation or conditions.

choices.text: The rate is zero at the very start
choices.why: At the start the reactants are at their highest concentrations, so the rate is not zero. The uncertainty comes from fluctuations in instrumentation or conditions.

choices.text: The rate law changes after the start
choices.why: The rate law holds throughout the reaction. The section's concern is fluctuations in instrumentation or conditions.

explanation: An initial-rate method rests on measurements made near the start of the reaction. Fluctuations in instrumentation or conditions can then cause a great deal of experimental uncertainty.

prompt: Some methods use a broad range of time and concentration data, the full concentration profile. Why do they tend to give more reliable results than initial-rate methods?

choices.text: Many data smooth over fluctuations
They need no calibration of the instrument
choices.why: Calibration is not the point. A broad range of data lets random fluctuations average out, which makes the result more reliable.

choices.text: They avoid the need for a rate constant
choices.why: These methods still give a rate constant. Their advantage is that the broad range of data smooths over random fluctuations.

choices.text: They are made before any product forms
choices.why: A full profile follows the reaction over a broad range of times, as products form. The many data smooth over random fluctuations.

explanation: A broad range of time and concentration data lets random fluctuations that affect single measurements average out. An initial rate rests on far fewer measurements, so one fluctuation can throw it off.
